newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH REFORMIST PARTY HITS ALL-TIME LOW IN POLLS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH REFORMIST PARTY HITS ALL-TIME LOW IN POLLS.

text.p: Poland's opposition Union for Freedom, one of the most pro-market-reform parties, has dropped so low in popularity that it would not to enter parliament if elections were held now, a public opinion poll showed on Friday.

The January poll by the public CBOS agency showed the Union -- which includes two former prime ministers, Tadeusz Mazowiecki and Hanna Suchocka -- would get four percent of the vote, one point less than the required threshold.
It is the first time in its history that the party, whose many members oversaw Poland's market reforms after the 1989 fall of communism, placed below the five-percent level.
CBOS said in a comment that the party's popularity was pulled down, from eight percent in December, by internal disputes about its political future and possible alliances.

Earlier this month, six prominent deputies left the Union to join a powerful newly formed bloc led by the Solidarity trade union. They said the bloc was the only group able to defeat the ruling ex-communists in elections due in September or October.
The CBOS poll showed the Solidarity bloc would snatch 25 percent of the vote while the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance, in power since the 1993 elections, would get 20 percent.
It indicated both groups had improved their ratings by two points since December.
The Polish Peasant Party, the junior partner in the government, would end up as the third strongest party in parliament, with a 10-percent support, according to the poll.

The survey, with a 3.2 percent error margin, showed three more parties would pass the five percent threshold -- the radical right Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland, the leftist Union of Labour and the Party of Pensioners.
